title: Grothendieck's existence theorem for proper schemes over a complete Noetherian ring
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] complete with respect to an ideal $I$ [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism] and $\mathcal I=I\mathcal O_X$ the image of $f^*\widetilde I\to\mathcal O_X$ [def-nagata-extended-ideal]. Then the completion functor $\mathit{Coh}(\mathcal O_X)\to\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$, $\mathcal F\mapsto\mathcal F^\wedge$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module], is an equivalence of categories: it is fully faithful, and every object $(\mathcal F_n)$ of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ is isomorphic to $\mathcal F^\wedge$ for some coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ [pqf-def-coherent].

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Proposition 088C (proposition-existence-proper), Section 0886 (section-existence-proper); its proof uses Lemma 0883 (lemma-fully-faithful), Chow's lemma 0200 (lemma-chow-Noetherian), the projective case Lemma 0885 (lemma-existence-projective), Lemma 088B (lemma-inverse-systems-push-pull) and Lemma 088A (lemma-existence-tricky); EGA III_1 Theorem 5.1.4

proof.text: (Setting; full faithfulness.) $\operatorname{Spec}A$ is a Noetherian scheme ($A$ Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]) and $f$ is proper, in particular of finite type [def-weil-proper-morphism], so $X$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]; the same holds for every scheme proper over $\operatorname{Spec}A$, so the categories $\mathit{Coh}(\mathcal O_Z)$ and $\mathit{Coh}(Z,I\mathcal O_Z)$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] are defined for every closed subscheme $Z$ of $X$ below. By [lem-weil-pbc-formal-completion-fully-faithful-proper] the completion functor $\mathit{Coh}(\mathcal O_X)\to\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ is fully faithful. So it suffices to show that it is essentially surjective, i.e. that every object of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ is isomorphic to $\mathcal F^\wedge$ for a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$; a fully faithful essentially surjective functor is an equivalence.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Proposition 088C (proposition-existence-proper), first paragraph, citing Lemma 0883 (lemma-fully-faithful)

proof.text: (Noetherian induction: the set $\Xi$.) For a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals $\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ let $i_{\mathcal K}:Z_{\mathcal K}\to X$ be the closed subscheme cut out by $\mathcal K$ [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-ideal-closed-subscheme] and $\mathcal I_{\mathcal K}=\mathcal I\mathcal O_{Z_{\mathcal K}}=I\mathcal O_{Z_{\mathcal K}}$ (extended ideals along a composite $W\to Y\to X$ agree: by [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-ideal-quotient] (1) both are, on affine opens, the ideal generated by the image of the sections of the ideal downstairs [def-nagata-extended-ideal]). $Z_{\mathcal K}\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is proper, as the composite of a closed immersion and a proper morphism [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (a),(c). Let $\Xi$ be the set of quasi-coherent ideals $\mathcal K$ such that every object of $\mathit{Coh}(Z_{\mathcal K},\mathcal I_{\mathcal K})$ is isomorphic to the completion of a coherent $\mathcal O_{Z_{\mathcal K}}$-module [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] (this does not depend on the choice of $Z_{\mathcal K}$, two choices being uniquely isomorphic over $X$ [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersions-equal-ideal-isomorphic], compatibly with the extended ideals). For $\mathcal K=(0)$ the identity of $X$ is a closed immersion with ideal $0$, so $Z_{(0)}\cong X$ over $X$ [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersions-equal-ideal-isomorphic] and $(0)\in\Xi$ is exactly the essential surjectivity to be proved. Suppose $(0)\notin\Xi$. The set of quasi-coherent ideals not in $\Xi$ is then nonempty, so as $X$ is Noetherian it has a maximal element $\mathcal K_0$ [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-acc-quasi-coherent]. Put $X_0=Z_{\mathcal K_0}$, $\iota:X_0\to X$, $\mathcal I_0=I\mathcal O_{X_0}$, and $f_0:X_0\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ (proper). $X_0\neq\emptyset$: otherwise $\mathit{Coh}(X_0,\mathcal I_0)$ has only zero objects, which are completions of the zero module, and $\mathcal K_0\in\Xi$. Every quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal L\supsetneq\mathcal K_0$ lies in $\Xi$ by maximality. We derive a contradiction by showing that every object $(\mathcal G_n)$ of $\mathit{Coh}(X_0,\mathcal I_0)$ is isomorphic to $\mathcal G^\wedge$ for a coherent $\mathcal O_{X_0}$-module $\mathcal G$ (steps 3-7), i.e. $\mathcal K_0\in\Xi$. (Stacks phrases $\Xi$ through the objects of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ annihilated by $\mathcal K$ and then replaces $X$ by $X_0$ using Lemma 087T; the version here works on the closed subschemes directly, which is the same by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-coherent-equivalence] (2).)

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Proposition 088C, second paragraph, citing Lemma 01Y8 (lemma-acc-coherent) and Lemma 087T (lemma-i-star-equivalence)

proof.text: (The induction hypothesis on $X_0$.) Claim: for every nonzero quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal K''\subseteq\mathcal O_{X_0}$, with $k:W\to X_0$ the closed subscheme it cuts out [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-ideal-closed-subscheme] and $\mathcal I_W=\mathcal I_0\mathcal O_W$, the completion functor $\mathit{Coh}(\mathcal O_W)\to\mathit{Coh}(W,\mathcal I_W)$ is an equivalence. Proof: $j=\iota\circ k:W\to X$ is a closed immersion [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-comp]; let $\mathcal L$ be its ideal sheaf [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. As $j$ factors through $\iota$, $\mathcal K_0\subseteq\mathcal L$ [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-factor-ideal-inclusion]. If $\mathcal L=\mathcal K_0$, then [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersions-equal-ideal-isomorphic] gives an isomorphism $\varphi:W\to X_0$ with $\iota\circ\varphi=\iota\circ k$; $\iota$ is a monomorphism (a closed immersion), so $k=\varphi$ is an isomorphism and its ideal $\mathcal K''=\ker(\mathcal O_{X_0}\to k_*\mathcal O_W)$ is $0$, a contradiction. So $\mathcal L\supsetneq\mathcal K_0$ and $\mathcal L\in\Xi$ (step 2). By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersions-equal-ideal-isomorphic] there is an isomorphism $\psi:W\to Z_{\mathcal L}$ with $i_{\mathcal L}\circ\psi=j$; it carries $\mathcal I_{\mathcal L}=I\mathcal O_{Z_{\mathcal L}}$ to $I\mathcal O_W=\mathcal I_0\mathcal O_W=\mathcal I_W$ (extended ideals along composites, as in step 2 [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-ideal-quotient] (1)), hence $\psi_*$ and $\psi^*$ identify coherent modules, the categories $\mathit{Coh}(\cdot,\cdot)$ and the completion functors of $(W,\mathcal I_W)$ and $(Z_{\mathcal L},\mathcal I_{\mathcal L})$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module]. Thus $\mathit{Coh}(\mathcal O_W)\to\mathit{Coh}(W,\mathcal I_W)$ is essentially surjective. $W\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is proper (closed immersion followed by the proper $f_0$ [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (a),(c)), so the functor is fully faithful [lem-weil-pbc-formal-completion-fully-faithful-proper], hence an equivalence.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Proposition 088C, second and last paragraphs ('we may assume that every nonzero K is in Xi'; 'the powers K^e are all in Xi so that the functor is an equivalence for the closed subschemes X_e = V(K^e)'), with Lemma 087T and Lemma 0883 for full faithfulness on X_e

proof.text: (Chow's lemma.) $f_0:X_0\to S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ is proper, so separated and of finite type, and $S$ is Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-chow-noetherian] there are $n\ge0$, a scheme $X'$, a proper surjective morphism $\pi:X'\to X_0$, an immersion $h:X'\to\mathbf P^n_A$ with $p\circ h=f_0\circ\pi$ ($p:\mathbf P^n_A\to S$ the projection), and a dense open $U\subseteq X_0$ with $\pi^{-1}(U)\to U$ an isomorphism. $f_0\circ\pi$ is proper [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence] (a); $p$ is proper [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper], in particular separated [def-weil-proper-morphism]; so $h$ is proper [lem-weil-pbc-proper-over-separated], in particular its image is closed (universally closed [def-weil-proper-morphism]), and the immersion $h$ with closed image is a closed immersion [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-closed-image-closed-immersion]. So $X'$ is a closed subscheme of $\mathbf P^n_A$ over $A$, and is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. (Stacks: $X'$ is H-projective over $A$.)

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Proposition 088C, third paragraph, citing Lemma 0200 (lemma-chow-Noetherian)

proof.text: (Projective case on $X'$.) Fix an object $(\mathcal G_n)$ of $\mathit{Coh}(X_0,\mathcal I_0)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-formal-systems-pullback] (1), $(\pi^*\mathcal G_n)$ is an object of $\mathit{Coh}(X',\pi^{-1}\mathcal I_0\cdot\mathcal O_{X'})$, and $\pi^{-1}\mathcal I_0\cdot\mathcal O_{X'}=I\mathcal O_{X'}$ (extended ideals along the composite $X'\to X_0\to S$, [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-ideal-quotient] (1), [def-nagata-extended-ideal]). As $X'$ is a closed subscheme of $\mathbf P^n_A$, [lem-weil-pbc-grothendieck-existence-projective] gives a coherent $\mathcal O_{X'}$-module $\mathcal F'$ and an isomorphism $(\mathcal F')^\wedge\cong(\pi^*\mathcal G_n)$ in $\mathit{Coh}(X',I\mathcal O_{X'})$; let $\beta:(\pi^*\mathcal G_n)\to(\mathcal F')^\wedge$ be its inverse.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Proposition 088C, third paragraph, citing Lemma 0885 (lemma-existence-projective); the pullback system is Lemma 0887 (lemma-inverse-systems-pullback)

proof.text: (Comparison with a proper pushforward.) Let $T=X_0\setminus U$ (closed) and $\mathcal K'\subseteq\mathcal O_{X_0}$ the ideal sheaf of the reduced induced closed subscheme on $T$ [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]; by its part (1), on an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R$ it is the radical ideal $J$ with $V(J)=T\cap\operatorname{Spec}R$, so $\{x:\mathcal K'_x\neq\mathcal O_{X_0,x}\}=T$ and $X_0\setminus V(\mathcal K')=U$, over which $\pi$ is an isomorphism. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-formal-systems-push-pull] with its $Y,\mathcal J,\mathcal K,f,X,\mathcal I,(\mathcal G_n),\mathcal F,\beta$ being $X_0,\mathcal I_0,\mathcal K',\pi,X',I\mathcal O_{X'},(\mathcal G_n),\mathcal F',\beta$ ($X_0$ Noetherian, $\pi$ proper): $\mathcal H=\pi_*\mathcal F'$ is a coherent $\mathcal O_{X_0}$-module, and there are a morphism $\alpha:(\mathcal G_n)\to\mathcal H^\wedge$ of $\mathit{Coh}(X_0,\mathcal I_0)$ and $t\ge1$ such that the kernel and cokernel of $\alpha$ in the abelian category $\mathit{Coh}(X_0,\mathcal I_0)$ [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-abelian] are annihilated by $\mathcal K'^t$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Proposition 088C, third paragraph, citing Proposition 02O5 (proposition-proper-pushforward-coherent) and Lemma 088B (lemma-inverse-systems-push-pull)

proof.text:
(The thickenings $V(\mathcal K'^e)$.) For $e\ge1$, $\mathcal K'^e
eq0$: $U$ is a dense open of the nonempty $X_0$, so $U
eq\emptyset$; $U\cap T=\emptyset$, so on every affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq U$ the radical ideal with empty zero set is $R$ [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] (1), i.e. $\mathcal K'|_U=\mathcal O_U$, hence $\mathcal K'^e|_U=\mathcal O_U$, which is nonzero as $U$ is a nonempty scheme ($R
eq0$ for a nonempty affine open). By step 3 applied to $\mathcal K''=\mathcal K'^e$, for every $e\ge1$ the completion functor $\mathit{Coh}(\mathcal O_{X_{0,e}})	o\mathit{Coh}(X_{0,e},\mathcal I_0\mathcal O_{X_{0,e}})$ is an equivalence, where $X_{0,e}\subseteq X_0$ is the closed subscheme cut out by $\mathcal K'^e$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, proof of Proposition 088C, last paragraph ('The powers K^e are all in Xi'); that K^e is nonzero is left implicit there

proof.text: (Conclusion.) $X_0$ is Noetherian, $\mathcal I_0,\mathcal K'\subseteq\mathcal O_{X_0}$ are quasi-coherent ideals, hypothesis (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-grothendieck-existence-devissage] holds by step 7 and hypothesis (2) by step 6 (with $\mathcal H$, $\alpha$, $t$). Hence there is a coherent $\mathcal O_{X_0}$-module $\mathcal G$ with $\mathcal G^\wedge\cong(\mathcal G_n)$. As $(\mathcal G_n)$ was arbitrary, $\mathcal K_0\in\Xi$, contradicting the choice of $\mathcal K_0$ (step 2). So $(0)\in\Xi$: the completion functor $\mathit{Coh}(\mathcal O_X)\to\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ is essentially surjective, and with step 1 it is an equivalence.
